messages:
Carla: Heads-up 1 CI linkcheck on the docs migration branch flagged two failures: a broken anchor and a weird parse hiccup inside a fenced code example. Error snippet:

Carla: ```
Linkcheck: docs/guides/migration.md#why-use-redwood -> anchor not found
Build: MkDocsParserWarning: raw HTML comment inside fenced code block at docs/examples/snippet.md:12
```

Ben: Which files are these pointing at exactly? I can't repro locally yet.

Carla: migration.md has a heading `## Why use Redwood? 🚀` which got slugified to `why-use-redwood-%F0%9F%9A%80` on newer MkDocs, but the link in older guides used `#why-use-redwood`. The snippet.md one contains an example showing an HTML comment inside a triple-backtick block: ````
```yaml
# sample config
# <!-- this comment is intentionally raw to show deployment hooks -->
hooks:
  - deploy
```
````
MkDocs warn/parse treats that differently depending on parser version.

Alice: Ah, emoji slug changes bite again. Options: 1) normalize all links to percent-encoded emoji slugs (ugh) 2) add an explicit id on the heading `## Why use Redwood? 🚀 {#why-use-redwood}` 3) avoid emoji in headings. For the code comment, easiest is to escape the `<!--` or show it as escaped text in the fenced example.

Ben: I'll do minimal patches: add `{#why-use-redwood}` to the heading in migration.md and escape the HTML comment in snippet.md by replacing `<!--` with `<!--` in the fenced example. That should be safe for backports too.

docs-ci: Note: If your local build uses an older mkdocs-material, the slug may differ. Backporting the explicit header id is the safest across branches.

Ben: Opening branch `docs/patch/emoji-heading-id-1799`. Ran local mkdocs build + linkcheck: all green. Pushed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/4981 :white_check_mark:

Carla: Nice. Please open a small backport PR to `release/v1.x` that only includes the `{#why-use-redwood}` header id (no other examples) so we don't risk churn on the release docs.

Ben: Will open `backport/docs-1799` right after merge.

Alice: I'll add a short note to CONTRIBUTING: "Avoid emoji in headings if you rely on slug stability; prefer explicit header ids for permanent links." Saves future surprises.

Carla: Thanks all 1 closing after backport merges.
